analysis_1_community_detection.description: Iterative algorithm where each node adopts the most frequent label among its neighbors. Converges when no node changes label.
pseudocode: INITIALIZE: assign unique label L[v] to each node v
FOR each node v in shuffled order:
label_counts = COUNT labels of all neighbors of v

communities.interpretation: Large general community anchored by wikipedia and sources nodes. These nodes share broad tag overlap (shared_tags edges) creating a densely connected core. Contains all 48 sources nodes, suggesting sources are tag-bridge connectors.

Operational core community. Contains the majority of SOPs and teams alongside knowledge-base entries. Held together by explicit_reference edges (builds_on/built_upon_by). This is the 'institutional knowledge' cluster.

Specialized wikipedia sub-cluster. These wiki nodes have stronger mutual connections than to the main cluster, suggesting a topically distinct sub-area (likely specific AI sub-topics that are more self-referential).

analysis_1_community_detection.domain_alignment_finding: Communities do NOT strongly align with domain types. Average entropy of 1.877 (max 2.81) shows moderate mixing. The network is organized more by topical/semantic relatedness than by domain type. This is expected since edges are created from shared_tags which cross domain boundaries.
recommendations: Use community structure to optimize routing: intra-community routes should be preferred for 1-hop lookups
Community 1 (operational core) should have higher default weights since it contains the most actionable content
Consider a hierarchical community approach: run label propagation within Community 0 to find sub-communities in the large 224-node cluster
Community membership could be stored as a node attribute to speed up route planning

analysis_2_pagerank.description: Iterative computation of node importance based on incoming link structure. Damping factor d=0.85. Weighted variant distributes rank proportional to edge weight rather than uniformly.
pseudocode: INITIALIZE: PR[v] = 1/N for all nodes v
sink_sum = SUM(PR[v]) for all v with out_degree=0
// Weighted variant: d * PR[u] * w(u,v) / sum_weights_out(u)

key_divergences: KB-0004 ranks #1 by PageRank but only #5 by degree centrality. Its incoming links come from other high-PageRank nodes, amplifying its importance.
SCR-0007 is #1 by degree (146 total) but #2 by PageRank. Many of its incoming links come from low-importance wiki nodes.
SCR-0018 is #2 by degree (144 total) but drops out of top 10 PageRank. Its high in-degree is inflated by many low-value connections.
TEAM-0014 (in_degree=53) appears at PageRank #8 despite not being in the degree top 15. It receives links from important knowledge-base nodes.
KB-0014 (in_degree=75) ranks PageRank #4 but degree #11. Its inbound links carry high authority.
pagerank_vs_degree_centrality_comparison.conclusion: PageRank reveals that knowledge-base nodes are more structurally important than raw degree suggests. SCR nodes accumulate many low-value inbound edges from wiki nodes, inflating their degree centrality. PageRank correctly identifies KB-0004 and KB-0005 as the true network hubs because they receive links from other authoritative nodes. Degree centrality overweights the 'popularity' of script nodes among wikipedia nodes.

recommendations: Use PageRank (not degree) for route prioritization: prefer routing through high-PR nodes
Weighted PageRank boosts KB nodes further, suggesting edge weights already encode quality signals
TEAM-0014 is a 'hidden hub' - important despite modest degree; ensure it is well-connected in routes
Consider PageRank as a multiplier on edge weights: w_effective = w * sqrt(PR_target / PR_mean)

algorithms.adamic_adar_index: AA(u,v) = SUM(1/log|N(w)|) for w in N(u) intersection N(v)

pseudocode: FOR each pair (u, v) where edge (u,v) does not exist:
AA = SUM(1 / log(degree(w)) for w in common)
IF AA > threshold: PREDICT edge (u,v) with confidence = AA

findings.intra_script_cluster: SCR-0006, SCR-0007, SCR-0008, SCR-0009, SCR-0010, SCR-0015, SCR-0018 form a near-clique with 90+ common neighbors between pairs but many missing direct edges. These scripts are clearly related and should be linked.
findings.cross_domain_gaps: The strongest cross-domain missing link is SCR-0018 -> KB-0005 (AA=32.65). This is as strong as most intra-script predictions, indicating a genuinely missing connection.
findings.jaccard_insight: SCR-0006 <-> SCR-0008 has Jaccard=0.968, meaning they share 96.8% of their neighborhoods. These are near-duplicate nodes topologically.

recommendations: Add edges for all pairs with Adamic-Adar > 25 and Jaccard > 0.5: approximately 15 edges
Prioritize cross-domain predictions (SCR-0018->KB-0005, KB-0005->SRC-0033) as they improve network integration
Suggested initial weight for predicted edges: weight = round(AA / 10), capped at 5
Run link prediction periodically after network updates to find emerging gaps
Investigate SCR-0006/SCR-0008 near-duplication: consider merging or differentiating

pruning_algorithm.name: Multi-Criteria Edge Pruning with Connectivity Guarantee

phases.name: Classify weight-1 edges
pseudocode: // If u and v share many other paths, this edge is redundant
IF cn_ratio > 0.5: score += 1  // already well-connected via neighbors
cross_domain_edges_u = count(edges from u to domain(v))
IF cross_domain_edges_u <= 2: score -= 2  // rare cross-domain link, keep it
IF pagerank(u) < median_pr AND pagerank(v) < median_pr:
score += 1  // edge between two unimportant nodes

phases.name: Connectivity-safe pruning
pseudocode: // Sort candidates by prune_score descending (most prunable first)
IF edge.prune_score < 2: BREAK  // only prune confident candidates
// Check if removing this edge disconnects any node
restore(edge)  // would leave a node too isolated

phases.name: Soft pruning (alternative to deletion)
phases.description: Instead of removing edges, mark them as 'dormant' with weight 0.5. They are excluded from default routing but can be reactivated if a route specifically needs them.
pseudocode: IF route_planner cannot find path with active edges only:
include dormant edges with penalty factor 2x

estimated_pruning_impact.routing_impact: Minimal - pruned edges are redundant paths between well-connected nodes

high_confidence_prune_category.description: Weight-1 shared_tags edges between nodes that already share 50+ common neighbors
high_confidence_prune_category.rationale: These nodes are already reachable via dozens of 2-hop paths. The weight-1 direct edge adds no routing value.

preserve_category.description: Weight-1 edges that serve as the only or one of few cross-domain bridges for a node
preserve_category.example: wiki nodes with in_degree=0 rely entirely on their outgoing weight-1 edges
preserve_category.rationale: 114 wiki nodes all have in_degree=0 and only 8 outgoing edges each. Pruning any reduces their already minimal connectivity.

recommendations: Start with soft pruning (dormant status) rather than deletion to allow recovery
Never prune edges from nodes with total_degree <= 8 (the wiki nodes)
Prioritize pruning within the dense SCR cluster where redundancy is highest
After pruning, re-run community detection to verify structure is preserved
Set up a pruning audit: if a dormant edge is reactivated 3+ times, restore it permanently
Target: reduce from 4820 to ~3800 active edges while maintaining diameter <= 4

composite_edge_score_formula.description: Recommended unified edge scoring for route planning
composite_edge_score_formula.formula: edge_score = (0.3 * normalized_weight) + (0.3 * pagerank_target / max_pagerank) + (0.2 * (1 - redundancy_ratio)) + (0.2 * success_rate)

components.success_rate: edge.success_count / edge.use_count (learned from route feedback, default 0.5)
